clue.text: Part of opening spell for oil producer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the second word of 'Open ...!', the magic command in Ali Baba
second meaning: a plant whose seeds are pressed for cooking oil

explanation.surface: Something like a magic word for striking oil, as if a prospector could chant a well into gushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening spell' looks like a first session of work, but it is the incantation that opens the robbers' cave in Ali Baba.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the plant grown for its oily seeds and completes the famous magic password from the Arabian Nights tale.

clue.text: Way to address girl in Essen or Italy? Yes and no

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their word breaks

parts.note: the tail of Essen, the whole of or and the start of Italy run together
surface comment and no letters: the word is in the phrase yet belongs to neither country, being Spanish

explanation.surface: A tourist wonders whether this greeting suits a young woman in a German city or in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' is the joke: the word is literally found in 'Essen or Italy', but it is Spanish, so it is no use in either country.
explanation.definitionFit: Senorita is the Spanish title for an unmarried young woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Forbidding gun when protecting monarch

indicators.note: protecting means guarding on every side, so the weapon wraps round the ruler

parts.note: the Sten gun, a British submachine gun
R for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A grim armed guard shielding the king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stern look is a severe, unapproachable one, so forbidding is a synonym in the sense of off-putting.

clue.text: Note what's said when hesitating as little as possible

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective use, as in 'minimum effort'

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, the half note
the sound a speaker makes when pausing for thought

explanation.surface: Someone saying very little, stalling with hums and haws.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimum describes the smallest amount allowed or possible, which is what the phrase spells out.

clue.text: Pick of bunch that'll make dough, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear rather than read, so the word wanted is one spoken the same as the thing described

parts.note: flour is mixed with water to make dough

explanation.surface: A baker choosing the best of a batch of ingredients for bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick of bunch' reads like the best item, and the answer means just that, as in 'the flower of the nation'; it is also literally in a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower of a group is its finest part, the choicest member, so it is the pick of the bunch.

clue.text: Inclined to provide entry in catalogue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: leaning to one side, as a ship does
second meaning: an item on a list

explanation.surface: Someone willing to supply an item for a sales brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' looks like 'willing', but it is the physical sense: tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lists is tilting over, and a listing is also a single item in a directory or catalogue.

clue.text: Water girl spilled is clearly visible

indicators.note: something spilled is scattered in disorder, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl carrying water has spilled it, and everyone can see.
explanation.definitionFit: Writ large is an idiom for something shown plainly or on a big scale, so obvious to see.

clue.text: Fan of loud music in seat person's crazy to vacate?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone devoted to rock music
second meaning: a rocking chair, from the idiom 'off one's ...' meaning mad

explanation.surface: A heavy-metal fan sitting in a chair that only a madman would leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Being crazy is 'off one's rocker', so the seat a crazy person has vacated is a rocking chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a rock-music enthusiast and a chair on curved runners, the one in the idiom for insanity.

clue.text: Detain alien that's useful source of information

parts.note: to intern is to confine, especially in wartime
the extraterrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: Holding a captured alien because of what it can tell you.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide computer network is where most people now look things up, a broad description rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Person looking for new stars ordered lens cut to a T

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new sequence, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomer hunting new stars has a lens ground precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: The astronomy picture misleads: the stars are performers, not suns.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent scout searches for promising new performers or players, the stars of the future.

clue.text: Current controller is small and charming woman

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a witch casts charms, and an enchanting woman is also called one

explanation.surface: Praise for a woman who is both petite and bewitching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day', but it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is the device that turns an electric current on or off, so it controls the flow.

clue.text: London architect that builds small home in country

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Christopher, who designed St Paul's Cathedral

definitions.text: that builds small home in country
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a tiny bird that makes its nest in the countryside

explanation.surface: A city architect who also puts up a cottage in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Builds small home' sounds like more architecture, but the builder is a bird making a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren rebuilt London's churches after the 1666 fire, and the wren is a small songbird that builds a domed nest.

clue.text: Finds product of reconstructed mill I set up

indicators.note: something reconstructed is rebuilt in a new form, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A manufacturer reports what a rebuilt mill turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Product' looks like manufactured goods, but it is the arithmetic result of multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the product is the result of multiplying numbers, so finding it is what one does when one multiplies.

clue.text: Surprise about a celebrity returning, one working in theatre

indicators.note: about means around, so one part wraps round the other

parts.note: to stagger is to astonish
taken as written

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so these words are read from right to left

parts.note: a big name is a famous person

explanation.surface: A famous star unexpectedly makes a comeback on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage manager runs the backstage side of a theatre production, so is a theatre worker.

clue.text: Name included by showy editor for added embellishment

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the adjective: with embellishment added

indicators.note: something included by another is held within it, so one part goes inside

parts.note: garish means gaudy, loudly showy
N is the abbreviation for name
the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A flamboyant editor adds a name as a flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish that is garnished has a decoration added, so the word describes something given extra adornment.

clue.text: Bank absorbing change in the US of late

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a small American coin, loose change

explanation.surface: An American bank that has lately been taking in small coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun for a financial institution, but it is the verb as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Of late is an idiom for in the recent past, so it means the same as lately.

clue.text: Is bloke held by Communists found out about again?

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped on both sides, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: two Reds, a Red being a communist; the pair hold the rest between them
taken as written
cove is old British slang for a man, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man captured by communists has been tracked down once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Communists' supplies two Reds, one either side of the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rediscover something is to find it once more, to learn of it again after it was lost.

clue.text: Bearer of welcome message in bold type? Far from it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the mat at the front door, often printed with 'Welcome'

definitions.text: in bold type? Far from it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a meek person who lets others walk over them, the opposite of a bold type

explanation.surface: A greeting printed in heavy lettering, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bold type' looks like typography, but a type is a kind of person; the opposite of a bold one is someone trodden on.
explanation.definitionFit: The mat by the door often bears the word Welcome, and a spineless person who is walked over is called by the same name.

clue.text: Employment initially cut — remedy is not clear

indicators.note: the beginning is cut off, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: jobs are work, employment
a cure remedies an illness

explanation.surface: Job cuts are announced, and the fix for them is uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means hard to understand or make out, so it is unclear.

clue.text: American women in English lake district

definitions.meaning: first meaning: US slang for women
second meaning: the Norfolk ..., a region of shallow lakes and waterways in eastern England

explanation.surface: American tourist women visiting the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake district' tempts toward the Lake District in Cumbria; the answer is the other watery region, in Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Broads is dated American slang for women, and the Broads are the network of shallow lakes in Norfolk and Suffolk.

clue.text: A tour riots disrupted? That's untrue

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A report that riots wrecked a tour is dismissed as false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untrue' reads as false, but here it means disloyal, untrue to one's country.
explanation.definitionFit: Traitorous means betraying one's side, and untrue in its older sense means unfaithful or disloyal.

clue.text: Part of stove, normally

indicators.note: part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the end of stove and the start of normally

explanation.surface: A cookery note that the oven is usually built into the cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the answer is literally part of 'stove, normally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooker usually combines a hob with an enclosed oven, so the oven is normally one part of a stove.

clue.text: Award presented in ring — reminder of painful fight

parts.note: the letter is ring-shaped
a mark left by a wound

explanation.surface: A boxer handed a trophy in the ring, carrying a mark from the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxing ring is the misdirection: it supplies only a round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the statuette given at the Academy Awards, the best-known film prize.

clue.text: Understand loud party being cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the end is chopped off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
an at-home is a reception held in one's house

explanation.surface: Making sense of a noisy party that ended early.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to get to the bottom of it, so to grasp or understand it.

clue.text: Reduce extent of, or otherwise cut a rent

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the following letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A landlord is urged to shrink a lease or else lower the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate is to shorten by cutting off part, so it reduces the length of something.

clue.text: Totally composed, at ease — or just partly

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the end of composed, all of at and the start of ease

explanation.surface: A person who is entirely calm and relaxed, or only somewhat so.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'composed, at ease' serve twice: taken whole they define the answer, taken in part they contain it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried, so a sedate person is entirely composed and relaxed.

clue.text: Daughter prematurely joined, at great expense

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
before the expected time

explanation.surface: A daughter who signed up too soon, and paid heavily for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dearly' here is in the sense of 'pay dearly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay dearly is to pay a high price, so the adverb means at great cost.
